extracted.intended_audience: users of the Singular computer algebra system (mathematicians / computer-algebra practitioners) working with the non-commutative subsystem and dmod libraries
extracted.subtask_description: Reference documentation for procedures in Singular's non-commutative (central.lib) and D-module (dmod.lib) libraries: usage signatures, return values, purposes, assumptions, notes, warnings and examples showing typical input/output and checks.

rubrics_metrics.name: scalarProd
rubrics_metrics.description: Usage: scalarProd(v,w); v,w intvecs. Return: int, the standard scalar product of v and w. Purpose: computes the scalar product of two intvecs. Assume: the arguments are of the same size.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Example given; no special notes.

rubrics_metrics.name: vec2poly
rubrics_metrics.description: Usage: vec2poly(v [,i]); v a vector or an intvec, i an optional int. Return: poly, a univariate polynomial in i-th variable with coefficients given by v. Purpose: constructs an univariate polynomial in K[var(i)] with given coefficients such that coefficient at var(i)^{j-1} is v[j].
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Note: optional i must be positive, default i=1. Examples show conversions from vector/intvec to polynomial.

rubrics_metrics.name: centralizeSet
rubrics_metrics.description: Usage: centralizeSet(F, V); F, V ideals or finite sets of elements of base algebra. Return: ideal, generated by computed elements. Purpose: computes a vector space basis of the centralizer of set F in the vector space generated by V over the ground field.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Example shows computing center via PBW_maxMonom then centralizeSet and verifying with inCenter. See related routines centralizer, centralizerVS, inCentralizer.

rubrics_metrics.name: centralizerVS
rubrics_metrics.description: Usage: centralizerVS(F, D); F ideal, D int. Return: ideal, generated by computed elements. Purpose: computes a vector space basis of centralizer(F) up to degree D.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Note: D must be non-negative. Example computes centralizer up to degree 4 and checks with inCentralizer. See centerVS, centralizer, inCentralizer.

rubrics_metrics.name: centralizerRed
rubrics_metrics.description: Usage: centralizerRed(F, D[, N]); F ideal, D int, N optional int. Return: ideal, generated by computed elements. Purpose: computes subalgebra generators of centralizer(F) up to degree D. In general the full centralizer may not be computable so termination must be specified by D and/or N.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Behavior: if D>0 compute up to degree D; if D<0 termination determined by N only; if N given, stops when at least N elements found but may not terminate if N exceeds actual number. Current ordering must be degree-compatible well-ordering. Example and cross references provided.

rubrics_metrics.name: centerVS
rubrics_metrics.description: Usage: centerVS(D); D int. Return: ideal, generated by computed elements. Purpose: computes a vector space basis of the center up to degree D.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Note: D must be non-negative. Example shows basis elements and checks inCenter. See center, centerRed, centralizerVS, inCenter.

rubrics_metrics.name: centerRed
rubrics_metrics.description: Usage: centerRed(D[, N]); D int, N optional int. Return: ideal, generated by computed elements. Purpose: computes subalgebra generators of the center up to degree D. Full center often not computable so termination via D and/or N required.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If D>0 compute up to degree D; if D<0 termination determined by N only; if N given, stops when at least N elements found but may not terminate if N too large. Example contrasts centerVS and centerRed results. See center, inCenter.

rubrics_metrics.name: center
rubrics_metrics.description: Usage: center(D[, N]); D int, N optional int. Return: ideal, generated by computed elements. Purpose: computes subalgebra generators of the center up to degree D. Same termination/behavior constraints as centerRed.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examples show computing center(3) and center(-1,1) to get at least one generator. Current ordering must be degree-compatible well-ordering. See centralizer, inCenter.

rubrics_metrics.name: centralizer
rubrics_metrics.description: Usage: centralizer(F, D[, N]); F poly/ideal, D int, N optional int. Return: ideal, generated by computed elements. Purpose: computes subalgebra generators of centralizer(F) up to degree D. Same general limitations as other 'Red' routines.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If D>0 compute up to degree D; if D<0 termination by N only; N may cause non-termination if too large. Example shows centralizer of a central polynomial returns algebra generators; another example for non-central polynomial. Use inCentralizer to check results.

rubrics_metrics.name: sa_reduce
rubrics_metrics.description: Usage: sa_reduce(V); V ideal. Return: ideal, generated by computed elements. Purpose: compute a subalgebra basis of an algebra generated by elements of V.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: At the moment limited to G-algebras. Example shows reduction of an ideal to expected subalgebra generators. See sa_poly_reduce.

rubrics_metrics.name: sa_poly_reduce
rubrics_metrics.description: Usage: sa_poly_reduce(p, V); p poly, V ideal. Return: polynomial, a reduction of p with respect to V. Purpose: computes a reduction of polynomial p w.r.t. the subalgebra generated by elements of V.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Currently limited to G-algebras. Example shows reduction of f+3*f*f+x with ideal(f) yields 'x'. See sa_reduce.

rubrics_metrics.name: inCenter
rubrics_metrics.description: Usage: inCenter(E); E poly/list/ideal. Return: integer, 1 if E is in the center, 0 otherwise. Purpose: check whether elements of E are central.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examples show usage on single polys, lists, ideals. Useful for verifying outputs of center/centerVS/centerRed.

rubrics_metrics.name: inCentralizer
rubrics_metrics.description: Usage: inCentralizer(E, S); E poly/list/ideal, S poly/ideal. Return: integer, 1 if E is in centralizer(S), 0 otherwise. Purpose: check whether elements of E are in centralizer(S).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examples include using printlevel to get verbose diagnostic output. Example shows output messages when element not in centralizer. Use to validate centralizer results.

rubrics_metrics.name: isCartan
rubrics_metrics.description: Usage: isCartan(f); f poly. Return: integer, 1 if f is a Cartan element, 0 otherwise. Purpose: check whether f is a Cartan element (i.e., for all g in A exists C in K s.t. [f,g]=C*g).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Example: central elements are Cartan; test for algebra U(sl_2). Explanation: equivalent condition can be checked on variables. Examples provided.

rubrics_metrics.name: applyAdF
rubrics_metrics.description: Usage: applyAdF(B, f); B ideal, f poly. Return: ideal generated by Ad f(B[i]) for 1<=i<=size(B). Purpose: apply Ad_f to every element of B where Ad_f(v) := [f,v] = f*v - v*f.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Example demonstrates computing images of PBW basis under Ad_e, constructing linear system and kernel, and checking Ad_e(K)=0. See linearMapKernel.

rubrics_metrics.name: linearMapKernel
rubrics_metrics.description: Usage: linearMapKernel(Images); Images ideal. Return: syzygy module, or int(0) if all images are zero. Purpose: computes syzygy module of linear map given by Images (i.e., kernel of linear map).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Example shows computing kernel of Ad_e by forming Images ideal with applyAdF then linearMapKernel then linearCombinations. If all images zero returns integer 0. See applyAdF and linearCombinations.

rubrics_metrics.name: linearCombinations
rubrics_metrics.description: Usage: linearCombinations(Basis, C); Basis ideal, C module. Return: ideal generated by computed linear combinations. Purpose: forms linear combinations of elements from Basis by replacing gen(i) by Basis[i] in C.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Used to convert syzygy module output to actual combinations of basis vectors; example shows retrieving kernel elements from syzygy module.

rubrics_metrics.name: variablesStandard
rubrics_metrics.description: Usage: variablesStandard(); Return: ideal, generated by algebra variables. Purpose: computes set of algebra variables taken in their natural order.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Example demonstrates natural order for variables. See variablesSorted.

rubrics_metrics.name: variablesSorted
rubrics_metrics.description: Usage: variablesSorted(); Return: ideal, generated by sorted algebra variables. Purpose: computes variables sorted so Cartan variables come first as a heuristic to speed center computation (compute centralizers of Cartan variables first to avoid solving systems).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Example: in U(sl_2) 'z' (Cartan) is placed first. See variablesStandard.

rubrics_metrics.name: PBW_eqDeg
rubrics_metrics.description: Usage: PBW_eqDeg(Deg); Deg int. Return: ideal consisting of found PBW elements of exactly given degree. Purpose: compute PBW elements of a given degree. Note: unit omitted; weights ignored.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Example lists PBW basis elements of degree==2. Useful for degree-restricted computations.

rubrics_metrics.name: PBW_maxDeg
rubrics_metrics.description: Usage: PBW_maxDeg(MaxDeg); MaxDeg int. Return: ideal consisting of found PBW elements up to MaxDeg. Purpose: compute PBW elements up to maximal degree. Note: unit omitted; weights ignored.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Example shows PBW_maxDeg(2) returning monomials of degree <=2. Useful for building bases for centralizer/center routines.

rubrics_metrics.name: PBW_maxMonom
rubrics_metrics.description: Usage: PBW_maxMonom(m); m poly. Return: ideal consisting of found PBW elements up to a given maximal monomial. Purpose: compute PBW elements up to a given maximal monomial. Note: unit omitted; weights ignored.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Example uses m = e*(f^2)*h to restrict exponents; then PBW_maxMonom returns list of monomials up to that bound. Useful to create PBW vector space V for centralizeSet etc.

rubrics_metrics.name: annfs
rubrics_metrics.description: Usage: annfs(f [,S,eng]); f a poly, S a string choosing algorithm, eng optional int. Return: ring. Purpose: compute the D-module structure of basering[1/f]*f^s (Ann F^s) with algorithm S and Groebner engine eng.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: S can be 'bm' (default, Briancon-Maisonobe), 'ot' (Oaku-Takayama), 'lot' (Levandovskyy modification). eng<>0 uses std, otherwise slimgb. Output ring contains LD (annihilator Groebner basis) and BS (roots/multiplicities of BS polynomial). Use setring to inspect output. printlevel controls verbosity. Example provided.

rubrics_metrics.name: annfspecial
rubrics_metrics.description: Usage: annfspecial(I,F,mir,n); I an ideal, F a poly, int mir, number n. Return: ideal. Purpose: compute annihilator ideal of F^n in Weyl algebra for given rational n, given Ann F^s in D[s] and minimal integer root mir of BS.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Assumes basering is D[s] containing s explicitly, I is Ann F^s (from SannfsBM), mir is minimal integer root, n rational. Computes annihilator for both generic and exceptional rational n per Saito-Sturmfels-Takayama algorithm. printlevel controls verbosity. Examples show several cases including exceptional root.

rubrics_metrics.name: Sannfs
rubrics_metrics.description: Usage: Sannfs(f [,S,eng]); f a poly, S a string, eng optional int. Return: ring. Purpose: compute D-module structure of basering[f^s] (Ann F^s) with chosen algorithm S and Groebner engine eng.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: S options same as annfs; eng handling same. Output ring contains LD (needed D-module structure). Use setring to view LD. printlevel controls debug messages. Example for x^3+y^3+z^3 provided.

rubrics_metrics.name: Sannfslog
rubrics_metrics.description: Usage: Sannfslog(f [,eng]); f a poly, eng optional int. Return: ring. Purpose: compute D-module structure of basering[1/f]*f^s; in output, LD1 is ideal generated by elements in Ann F^s coming from logarithmic derivations.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: eng handling same as other annfs routines. printlevel controls verbosity. Example shows LD1 output containing elements coming from logarithmic derivations.

rubrics_metrics.name: bernsteinBM
rubrics_metrics.description: Usage: bernsteinBM(f [,eng]); f a poly, eng optional int. Return: list (roots of Bernstein polynomial and multiplicities). Purpose: compute global Bernstein–Sato polynomial for hypersurface defined by f using Briancon–Maisonobe algorithm.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: eng handling: eng<>0 uses std; otherwise slimgb. printlevel controls verbosity. Examples show returned list of rational roots with multiplicities.

rubrics_metrics.name: bernsteinLift
rubrics_metrics.description: Usage: bernsteinLift(I, F [,eng]); I an ideal, F a poly, eng optional int. Return: list. Purpose: compute (multiple of) Bernstein–Sato polynomial with lift-like method based on Sannfs-like output.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Output list contains candidate roots with multiplicities; not necessarily normalized BS polynomial. Use fl2poly to convert list to polynomial. eng & printlevel behavior as usual. Example shows converting to polynomial and candidate roots.

rubrics_metrics.name: operatorBM
rubrics_metrics.description: Usage: operatorBM(f [,eng]); f a poly, eng optional int. Return: ring. Purpose: compute B-operator and other relevant data for Ann F^s using (e.g.) BM algorithm: yields LD (Ann f^s), LD0 (annihilator at s0), bs (Bernstein polynomial), BS (roots/multiplicities), and PS (operator with PS*f^(s+1)=bs*f^s).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Activate output ring with setring to inspect F, LD, LD0, bs, BS, PS. eng and printlevel as usual. Example shows checking PS property by reduce(PS*F-bs,LD) -> 0. Useful combined routine to obtain all relevant D-module data.

rubrics_metrics.name: operatorModulo
rubrics_metrics.description: Usage: operatorModulo(f,I,b); f a poly, I an ideal, b a poly. Return: poly. Purpose: compute B-operator from polynomial f, ideal I = Ann f^s and Bernstein polynomial b using modulo (kernel of module homomorphism) method.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Computation in ring similar to Sannfs output. Operator may not be completely reduced w.r.t. Ann f^{s+1}; example shows further reduction using NF and subst(LD,s,s+1). printlevel controls verbosity. Example demonstrates extraction and checks via reduce(PS*F-bs,LD) -> 0.

rubrics_metrics.name: annfsParamBM
rubrics_metrics.description: Usage: annfsParamBM(f [,eng]); f a poly with parametric coefficients, eng optional int. Return: ring. Purpose: compute generic Ann F^s and exceptional parametric constellations of polynomial with parameters using BM algorithm.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Output ring contains LD (D-module structure) and Param (special parameters). eng and printlevel as before. Activate output ring with setring. Example referenced.
